title: Add ability to rewrite database cached paths
body:
Right now, the only way to change a cached path is to completely remove the database - `podman system reset`. There are good reasons why this was done historically - we have some of these paths in the database, and changing the graphroot on disk while having these paths still in the database is guaranteed to break something. These justifications don't really make sense when we don't have any objects in the database, however. If the DB is empty of pods/volumes/containers, it should be safe to rewrite the cached paths.

This PR makes that rewrite automatic. It also does a bit of a refactor on how we do path validation in the first place. Previously, a single validation failure halted the entire process. Now, we use a multierror so all validation failures are reported and the user gets the full picture of the mismatch.

I haven't added a message to "remove all pods and containers and volumes to fix this" in the error message, but that might be a good idea.

<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

<!--
Write `None` if there are no user-facing changes, otherwise enter your release note below.
Include "action required" if users need to take action when upgrading.
-->

```release-note
Database cached path validation now only occurs when containers, pods, and volumes are present. As a result, a `podman system reset` is no longer necessary to handle a change in paths in use if all containers, pods, and volumes are removed.
```
